WHAT IS NOT REALLY THERE — say this before the interviewer finds it
ONE-FIELD STUB CLASSES — compiled, never used
Quiz { quizId } · Assignment { assignmentId } · Progress { progressId }
Each is a single id + getter. Nothing constructs them, nothing stores them.
Consequence: a Quiz has no questions, so submitAssessment CANNOT grade —
which is exactly why the impl falls back to Math.random().
Fix in the interview: give Quiz a List<Question> with correctIndex, then grading is a fold.
Students and instructors live only as opaque id Strings in the maps — no user model at all.

g.text: COMPOSITION vs REFERENCE — the one modelling call
Course OWNS its lessons (List<Lesson>): delete the course and the
lessons are meaningless. That is composition, so hold the objects.
Course REFERENCES its instructor (instructorId: String): the instructor
outlives the course and is shared by many. Hold an id, not a pointer.
Same rule for Enrollment: it references BOTH sides by id, because it is
a join row, not an owner. Getting this split right is most of the design.
WHY enrollStudent IS THE ONLY synchronized METHOD
ConcurrentHashMap makes each individual put and get atomic. Enrolment is not one
operation though — it is check duplicate → count capacity → write two maps. Two threads
can both pass a capacity check for the last seat and both enrol. Classic check-then-act.
So the compound operation gets a lock; the simple reads stay lock-free. Correct reasoning ✓
But the lock is on the whole SERVICE, so enrolling in "Java 101" blocks enrolling in "Go 201".
Upgrade: lock per courseId, or hold an AtomicInteger seat counter on Course and CAS it down.
